name: Threat Model Reviewer v2.0.3
body_html:
Threat Model Reviewer v2.0.3

Release date: 9 August 2026 · Platform: Windows 10/11 x64 · Type: Patch — documentation
and product copy. No functional change.

Threat Model Reviewer reviews, fixes and analyzes Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool (.tm7) threat
models — and OWASP Threat Dragon (.json) — catching the issues a Microsoft SDL reviewer would
send back before you submit. The readiness verdict and 0–100 score are deterministic and
computed entirely on your machine.

At a glance

Item Detail
What changed Product copy and documentation now describe exactly the capabilities that ship today
Who should update Everyone — this is the current supported release
Risk of updating Minimal: no engine, verdict, scoring or file-format changes
Downtime / migration None. Settings, credentials and preferences are preserved
Rollback Install any earlier 2.0.x package; configuration is forward/backward compatible

Changed

  • Product copy now matches the shipped feature set. The header subtitle, About dialog, package
    description and documentation previously described the app as also creating threat models.
    Model authoring is in beta and hidden in the desktop build, so every surface now reads
    "review, fix & analyze", and the Create capability — a guided wizard, plus Copilot drafting a
    data-flow diagram from a description, an architecture image or an OpenAPI spec — is clearly
    labelled beta.

    The create and openapi commands remain available in the CLI today for teams that want
    to author models programmatically.

  • Documentation raised to enterprise standard. New and expanded material for security review
    and managed rollout:

    • Data handling & privacy — every network destination, every on-disk path, the secret
      redaction applied before any AI prompt, and confirmation that the product collects no
      telemetry.
    • Enterprise deployment — silent install switches, MSI UpgradeCode and Inno AppId for
      detection rules, Intune / Configuration Manager / Group Policy guidance, how to disable update
      checks fleet-wide, air-gapped operation, and CI/CD gating with the CLI.
    • Third-party notices — full component inventory with licenses.
    • Security policy — vulnerability response targets, a supported-versions table, and the
      controls protecting the tool itself (untrusted-file parsing, prompt-injection detection,
      DPAPI credential storage, export formula-injection neutralization, supply chain).
    • Support policy — severity definitions and response targets.

Unchanged and guaranteed

  • The verdict and 0–100 review score remain 100% deterministic — produced by a fixed
    rubric engine with no AI dependency. Copilot is advisory only.
  • The full review works offline. No network access is required.
  • Your threat model never leaves your machine. AI features send only finding text and a
    redacted structural summary, never the .tm7 itself.

What ships in this release

Open a .tm7 or Threat Dragon .json and you get a stamped NOT READY / READY WITH NOTES
verdict, a 0–100 score with a letter grade, and a prioritized findings list — from roughly 70
deterministic checks spanning completeness and structure, STRIDE coverage, triage and mitigation
quality, security hygiene, and the AI/agentic surface (OWASP LLM Top 10 2025, OWASP Agentic,
MITRE ATLAS). Plus: an interactive diagram with write-back, a previewable remediation plan that
saves a corrected .tm7 which reopens cleanly in the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool, deep
analysis (DREAD, attack trees, verification tests), and exports to HTML, PDF, Markdown, CSV,
JSON, SARIF and GitHub / Azure DevOps / Jira work items.

Updating

On v1.0.4 or later, the app updates itself: click Download & install on the in-app banner,
then Install & restart. Otherwise download a package below.

Administrators deploying centrally should follow
Enterprise deployment.

Downloads

Package Choose it when
…-x64.msi Standard installer; per-machine or per-user. Recommended, and the option for managed deployment
…-win-x64-portable.zip Extract and run — no installation
…-setup.exe Per-user installer, no administrator rights
…-x64.msix + …-publisher.cer MSIX (experimental — trust the .cer first; AI may be limited under MSIX)

Every build is self-contained — no .NET runtime installation required.
→ Install instructions

Verifying this release

Every artifact is Authenticode-signed. Before deploying widely:

Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\ThreatModelReviewer-v2.0.3-x64.msi | Format-List Status, SignerCertificate
Get-FileHash .\ThreatModelReviewer-v2.0.3-x64.msi -Algorithm SHA256

Artifacts are currently signed with a self-signed certificate (CN=ArasaniRohithReddy), so
Microsoft Defender SmartScreen may warn on first run — More info → Run anyway. Migration to a
CA/EV certificate or Azure Trusted Signing is planned and will require no change on the client.

Compatibility

Requirement Supported
Operating system Windows 10 (1809+) and Windows 11, x64
Runtime None required — self-contained
Input formats Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool .tm7; OWASP Threat Dragon .json
Optional AI GitHub Copilot (Individual / Business / Enterprise), or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including Azure OpenAI

Support

  • Bugs and ideas — open an issue
  • Vulnerabilities — report privately, never in a public issue

Full history: CHANGELOG

name: Threat Model Reviewer v2.0.0
body_html:
Threat Model Reviewer v2.0.0

A correctness release. Models you fix in the app now reliably reopen in the Microsoft Threat
Modeling Tool, Copilot's advisory text renders properly, and a whole-app audit (run with
Claude Opus 4.8 + Opus 5) hardened every write path.

Fixed

  • App-fixed .tm7 files now open in the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool. Two defects had
    made TMT reject a saved model as "could not be deserialized… or the threat model may be
    corrupted"    : the threat State was written in a human-readable form ("Needs Investigation")
    where TMT's enum requires the exact member name (NeedsInvestigation), and whole-model threats
    wrote empty GUID fields. Both are fixed and verified against TMT's own loader.
  • Fixed a TMT dashboard crash — "an item with the same key has already been added." TMT
    identifies a threat by TypeId + Source + Flow + Target, so several distinct threats added to a
    single element/category (for example multiple OWASP-LLM risks) now get distinct TypeIds and never
    collide.
  • The --baseline Create path no longer produces corrupt files (an XML declaration/encoding
    mismatch). The carried KnowledgeBase and multi-line names are preserved exactly.
  • Copilot output renders as formatted text. The whole-model critique, per-finding guidance, and
    mitigation plan now show real bold, italic, code, and bullet lists instead of literal
    ** and backticks.

Hardened (whole-app audit)

  • AI responses that are malformed, truncated, or fail entirely no longer crash the app or abort
    the deterministic report/verdict     — Copilot stays strictly advisory.
  • A triage-state parser no longer reads "not mitigated" / "needs mitigation" as Mitigated.
  • Model parsing, diff, and critique are robust to duplicate or blank element ids.
  • The portable-update helper can no longer hang invisibly; export CSVs are protected against
    spreadsheet formula-injection; the bundled Copilot runtime is never orphaned on exit.
  • Newly added diagram elements default in scope (a cloned template could previously flip them
    out-of-scope and change the deterministic result).

Determinism

The verdict and 0–100 review score remain 100% deterministic and are never influenced by
Copilot. Copilot only adds advisory guidance, critique, and drafted fixes that you choose to apply.

Updating

name: Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.9
body_html:
Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.9

Fixes "Check for updates" wrongly reporting you're up to date.

What's fixed

  • The update check no longer misreports "You're on the latest version" when it actually failed.
    GitHub's unauthenticated API is limited to 60 requests/hour per network; when that limit was hit
    (HTTP 403), the app treated the failure as "up to date" — so a genuinely newer version wasn't
    offered.
    • It now falls back to the releases.atom feed (served from github.com and not subject to
      that API rate limit), so update checks keep working even when the API is throttled.
    • If GitHub really can't be reached, it now says "Couldn't reach GitHub… try again later"
      instead of claiming you're on the latest version.

If you were stuck on an older build that kept saying "you're on the latest," this release fixes it —
update once and future checks are reliable.

body_html:
Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.8

Sign in to GitHub Copilot inside the app — no external CLI needed — while still using your
existing Copilot CLI sign-in when you have one.

What's new

  • In-app GitHub sign-in (device flow). Not signed in? Click Sign in to Copilot in the header
    and a dialog shows a one-time code. Click Copy code & open GitHub, approve it in your browser,
    and the app connects and lists your models. It's the same OAuth device flow and client the
    GitHub Copilot CLI uses     — you don't need the CLI installed, and there's no token to paste.

How authentication works (best UX first)

  1. Already signed in via the Copilot CLI (copilot login) or GitHub CLI (gh auth login)?
    The app uses that automatically — nothing to do.
  2. Not signed in? Use the in-app Sign in to Copilot device flow above.
  3. Headless / automation? Set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or GITHUB_TOKEN to a
    fine-grained PAT with the "Copilot Requests" permission.

You need an active GitHub Copilot subscription (Individual, Business, or Enterprise) for the AI
features. The deterministic review — verdict, 0–100 score, findings, and exports — needs none of
this and works fully offline. Copilot is advisory only.

name: Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.1
body_html:

name: Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.0
body_html:
Threat Model Reviewer v1.0.0

First public release — a Windows desktop tool that reviews, fixes, analyzes, and
creates Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool (.tm7) threat models, powered by your own
GitHub Copilot seat. The verdict and 0–100 score are deterministic (never produced
by AI); Copilot is optional and advisory.

Downloads

Download Use it if…
...-win-x64-portable.zip You want the simplest option — extract and run. (recommended)
...-setup.exe You want a Start-Menu shortcut + uninstall entry (per-user, no admin).
...-x64.msix + ...-publisher.cer You prefer MSIX (experimental — AI features may be limited under MSIX sandboxing; trust the .cer first).

See install instructions.
No .NET install needed — every download is self-contained.

Highlights

  • Deterministic verdict + 0–100 review score with ~70 grounded rubric checks (structural,
    STRIDE coverage, triage/mitigation quality, identity/boundary, data protection, network,
    logging/detection, deprecated crypto, supply chain, mismodeled stencils, and a deep
    AI/agentic surface — OWASP LLM Top 10 2025, OWASP Agentic, MITRE ATLAS).
  • STRIDE coverage matrix, Threats-by-interaction, and a Framework coverage
    scorecard (OWASP Top 10 + STRIDE).
  • Fix with round-trip write-back to a valid .tm7; Create via a wizard or Copilot
    DFD extraction.
  • Optional Copilot enrichments (explain, deep analysis, draft fixes, critique, gap
    analysis, triage planning) — each independent and advisory.
  • Exports: HTML / PDF / Markdown / CSV / JSON / SARIF + work items (GitHub / Azure
    DevOps / Jira).

Notes

  • The portable .exe and installer aren't Authenticode-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn
    on first run — More info → Run anyway.
  • Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue.
